rows.name: TRON_LINT_CLOSURE_PATHS
rows.table: 4.4 Tests of Dice, Slice and CI scripts

cells.Values and default: Path of a text file with one Nix store path (a path below `/nix/store`) on each line. Unset: the test fails with `Recursive lint closure manifest is missing` when `TRON_REQUIRE_CLOSURE_AUDIT` is `1`. Otherwise the test does not read it.
cells.Effect: The test reads the list of store paths in this file. It fails when no line equals the path in `TRON_EXPECTED_NIXFMT_PATH`. It also fails when the list holds the path in `TRON_SOURCE_STORE_PATH`, a first-party package or a `lefthook` package. A first-party package has `tron`, `runtron`, `rinzler`, `tokenize_py`, `tokenize-py` or `positron` as a whole part of its name, with `-` as the separator. `flake.nix` sets the variable to the `store-paths` file of `lintClosureInfo` in the Nix check `lint-toolchain` (a Nix build that runs this test).

rows.name: TRON_LINT_RUNTIME_CLOSURE_PATHS
rows.table: 4.4 Tests of Dice, Slice and CI scripts

cells.Values and default: Path of a text file with one Nix store path (a path below `/nix/store`) on each line. Unset: the test fails with `Recursive lint runtime closure manifest is missing` when `TRON_REQUIRE_CLOSURE_AUDIT` is `1`. Otherwise the test does not read it.
cells.Effect: The test searches this file for a line with a path part that contains `-ghc-` or `-cabal-install-` followed by a digit. On a match the test fails with `Lint runtime includes GHC, its documentation, or Cabal`. `flake.nix` sets it to the `store-paths` file of `lintRuntimeClosureInfo` in the Nix check `lint-toolchain` (a Nix build that runs this test).

rows.name: TRON_NIX_LEFTHOOK
rows.table: 4.4 Tests of Dice, Slice and CI scripts

cells.Values and default: Absolute path of an existing file. The test expects the wrapper script of Lefthook (the program that runs the Git pre-commit checks). Unset: the test class stops in `setUpClass` with `KeyError`. None of its tests runs.
cells.Effect: Names the Lefthook wrapper under test. The test passes the path to `bin/install-nix-hooks.py --lefthook`. One test case also runs `<path> install`. A relative path or a missing file raises `RuntimeError`. The test class also reads `shellHook` without a default. `flake.nix` sets `TRON_NIX_LEFTHOOK` in the lint dev shell that `nix develop .#lint` starts. `bin/ci/test-lint-check-regressions.sh` starts this test.

rows.name: TRON_REQUIRE_CLOSURE_AUDIT
rows.table: 4.4 Tests of Dice, Slice and CI scripts

cells.Values and default: Only the exact text `1` turns the audit on. Any other text behaves like unset. Unset: the test skips the closure audit, the `ghc` and `cabal` check and the `make lint-notes` check. Its tool path and version checks still run.
cells.Effect: With `1`, the test runs the closure audit (a check of the Nix store paths that the lint tools depend on). It also fails when `ghc` or `cabal` is on `PATH`, and it runs `make lint-notes` on a sample file. With `1`, the test needs `TRON_LINT_CLOSURE_PATHS`, `TRON_EXPECTED_NIXFMT_PATH` and `TRON_LINT_RUNTIME_CLOSURE_PATHS`. `TRON_SOURCE_STORE_PATH` is optional. The test stops earlier unless `TRON_NIX_LINT_SHELL` is `1`. `flake.nix` sets `1` in the Nix check `lint-toolchain` (a Nix build that runs this test).

rows.name: TRON_SOURCE_ROOT
rows.table: 4.4 Tests of Dice, Slice and CI scripts

cells.Values and default: Path of a directory that holds Tron source files. Unset: each test uses the checkout that holds the test file. Empty: the shell test does the same. The Python test uses the current directory.
cells.Effect: Selects the source tree that the two Rust toolchain tests use. The shell test reads `rust-toolchain.toml`, build files and `rust/` scripts from it. The Python test runs `rust/run-cargo-test-binary` from it. `flake.nix` sets it in the Nix check `rust-toolchain` (a Nix build that runs both tests). The shell test gets the flake source. The Python test gets a temporary directory with copies of `rust/run-cargo` and `rust/run-cargo-test-binary`.

rows.name: TRON_SOURCE_STORE_PATH
rows.table: 4.4 Tests of Dice, Slice and CI scripts

cells.Values and default: Nix store path (a path below `/nix/store`) of the repository source. The test compares it as exact text with each whole line of a file. Unset: the test does not look for a source path in the list. The test reads it only when `TRON_REQUIRE_CLOSURE_AUDIT` is `1`.
cells.Effect: The test fails with `Public lint closure contains repository source path` when a line of the file that `TRON_LINT_CLOSURE_PATHS` names equals this path. `flake.nix` sets it to `self.outPath` (the store path of the flake source) in the Nix check `lint-toolchain` (a Nix build that runs this test).

cells.Values and default: Integer, parsed with `atoi`. A value above `15` counts as `15`. A value of `0` or below counts as `15`. Text that is not a number counts as `15`. Unset: `15`. This is also the largest factor.
cells.Effect: Sets the factor that multiplies the iteration counts of 5 subtests of `t_fuse_sysfs`. A subtest is one named test function of that program. A factor below `15` lowers these counts. The 5 subtests are `ReadOnlyHostUpdates`, `HostConcurrentSetValue`, `ValidationAndConcurrentWrites`, `PollingUnderLoad` and `GlobalCallbackChurn`. Their base counts are 200, 1500, 1000, 2000 and 800 iterations, in that order. The variable cannot raise the counts above the default.

cells.Values and default: Path of a directory that holds the Perfetto programs `traced` and `perfetto`. Unset: the test `test_launchers_do_not_start_targets_before_perfetto_is_ready` stops with `KeyError`.
cells.Effect: The test `test_launchers_do_not_start_targets_before_perfetto_is_ready` starts the real `traced` and `perfetto` from this directory. `flake.nix` sets it for the Nix check `perfetto-config`. That check runs `perfetto/test_perfetto.py`. The other tests of that file do not read it.

cells.Values and default: Integer, parsed with `atoi`. A value below `1` counts as `1`. Text that is not a number counts as `1`. Unset: `1`. Each request table runs 1 time.

rows.name: CMAKE_DEFINES
rows.table: 5.1 `GNUmakefile` and the scripts that it runs

cells.Values and default: Any text. `GNUmakefile` only prints it. `make CMAKE_DEFINES=value` also works. Unset: the printed value is empty.
cells.Effect: Nothing changes in the build. When `DEBUG` is set, `make` prints the line `CMAKE_DEFINES = <value>` while it parses `GNUmakefile`. No rule passes the value to CMake. `GNUmakefile` never assigns this variable.

rows.name: DEBUG
rows.table: 5.1 `GNUmakefile` and the scripts that it runs

cells.Values and default: `GNUmakefile`: any non-empty text counts as set, `0` included. `bin/iotools-1.5/Makefile`: `0` selects the optimised build, and any other text selects the debug build. `make DEBUG=1` also works. Unset: `GNUmakefile` prints no extra lines. `bin/iotools-1.5/Makefile` uses `1`, the debug build with `-O0 -ggdb`.
cells.Effect: `GNUmakefile` prints the values of `BUILD_TYPE`, `MAKEFLAGS`, `TESTS`, `PHONY`, `RUN` and `CMAKE_DEFINES` while it parses, and changes nothing else. In `bin/iotools-1.5/Makefile` (the makefile of iotools, a third-party I/O tool copied into the repository), `0` compiles with `-O2 -DNDEBUG`. The two makefiles use the same name for different purposes. A `DEBUG` that is exported for another tool also turns on the `GNUmakefile` output. No Tron build file runs the iotools makefile.
